analysis: Integration pass over the PR: no runtime provider, coordinator, attestation, key-custody, encryption or cache-storage code changed. The changes are: (1) .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py LifecycleTests.setUp pins GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT="1" in the test env; the rerun-disabled test still overrides it to "2", so coverage of that guard remains. (2) .github/workflows/release-provider.yml adds job-level env DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT: prod to qualify-sdk (head ~236-242) and updates a comment at lines 178-182. build-provider still uses the resolve-env output, so the signed artifact's environment identity is unchanged. qualify-sdk keeps contents: read, has no secrets, and the value is a hard-coded literal, not derived from untrusted input. Signing, notarization, publication and secret-scoped jobs are untouched. (3) docs/operations/provider-release.md and changelog.d/qualify-sdk-prod-identity.md document the change. (4) scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py tightens the pipeline test: qualify-sdk must name the variable exactly once, at job-level env, with literal prod, and must not use the resolved-env selector. This hardens against dev/staging identity drift in the qualification lane. Related threat IDs: A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054 only tangentially; no control is weakened and no new attack surface is added. Unverified contracts, outside supplied evidence: the provider-release-build composite action's handling of lane=qualification and its environment input, and Package.swift env selection. If the action overrides the job-level value, the effect would be a test-fidelity failure that the new pipeline test only partially detects, not a security regression. Whether any qualification output is consumed as a release gate or artifact is not visible; existing DAG tests indicate it is not signed or published. No findings.
